folder.title: From resident research to a map, a poster, and a community lecture.
folder.copy: Questionnaire summaries and presentation pages sit beside three responses developed from the study. A printed map draft organizes nearby facilities by walking time. A food-safety poster addresses misconceptions about leftovers, while anti-fraud lecture notes translate survey gaps into practical guidance for older residents.

facts.label: MAP DRAFT
facts.value: facility markers · category filters · 5 / 10 / 15-minute walking zones

facts.label: FOOD-SAFETY POSTER
facts.value: leftover-related health risks · misconception correction · community distribution

facts.label: ANTI-FRAUD LECTURE
facts.value: fraud recognition · property protection · qualitative resident feedback

folder.note: The packet preserves two kinds of response to the same research: a digital tool for finding nearby services and community materials for information gaps identified during the study.

notebook.meta: THERMO FISHER / ROBOTIC TUBE HANDLING / TEST PACKET
notebook.title: Three model iterations for a four-class perception-to-action workflow.
notebook.copy: A working packet of robot-camera captures, Roboflow exports, training runs, held-out comparisons, and saved real-hardware workflow frames. It traces the detector from three classes to four and the system from perception-only tests to verified pickup and placement.
notebook.note: Remaining unsuccessful runs involved intermittent camera or hardware faults. Recovery tooling restores operation, but the root cause remains unresolved.

components.meta: EMG DEVICE / HARDWARE ITERATION / REV. CURRENT
components.title: The enclosure had to shrink around the electronics.
components.copy: Built and soldered the signal path, then arranged the ESP32 boards and battery inside a compact wearable enclosure. The body and lid reserve openings for the power switch and charging port so the device can be operated and recharged while assembled.
components.note: The hardware prototype is assembled and operational. Software behavior, data analysis, and the user interface still require further development.

envelope.title: No method led every criterion.
envelope.copy: Compared First-Come-First-Serve, Random Ticket, and probabilistic assignment with maximum-weight realization. FCFS required the least CPU time. Random Ticket made the final outcome harder to predict. The probabilistic approach produced the strongest reported satisfaction result.

facts.label: EVALUATION
facts.value: satisfaction mean + standard deviation · assignment completion · capacity violations

envelope.note: These tradeoffs motivated a mechanism that balanced limited course capacity across automation, efficiency, fairness, and overall student satisfaction. Fairness is presented here as an original project criterion, not as a formally proven guarantee.
